questions.title: How do you manage system events, incidents, and problems?
questions.description: In mission-critical environments, effective management of system events, incidents, and problems is crucial for maintaining operational readiness, protecting sensitive information, and ensuring mission success. A structured approach to event management helps prevent escalation of incidents and enables rapid response to maintain operational capabilities. (Aligns with AWS Well Architected Framework question Operational Excellence #10)

choices.title: Automate responses to events

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement automated response procedures for common events to reduce response time and ensure consistency.

helpfulResource.displayText: Automated responses help ensure rapid and consistent handling of events.

choices.title: Communicate status through dashboards

improvementPlan.displayText: Develop comprehensive dashboards that provide real-time visibility into system status and events.

helpfulResource.displayText: Dashboards provide critical visibility into system health and event status.

choices.title: Define a customer communication plan for outages

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish clear communication procedures and templates for different types of outages.

helpfulResource.displayText: A well-defined communication plan ensures stakeholders stay informed during incidents.

choices.title: Define escalation paths

improvementPlan.displayText: Document clear escalation procedures including contact information and response time expectations.

helpfulResource.displayText: Clear escalation paths ensure critical events receive appropriate attention and response.

choices.title: Prioritize operational events based on business impact

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement event prioritization based on mission impact and resource criticality.

helpfulResource.displayText: Event prioritization ensures critical issues receive immediate attention.

choices.title: Have a process per alert

improvementPlan.displayText: Develop and document specific response procedures for each type of alert.

helpfulResource.displayText: Having specific processes for each alert type ensures consistent and appropriate responses.

choices.title: Use a process for event, incident, and problem management

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish comprehensive event management processes aligned with operational excellence principles.

helpfulResource.displayText: A structured event management process is fundamental to operational excellence.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Select this if none of the above event management practices are implemented.

questions.title: How do you manage cloud support engagement and escalation processes?
questions.description: Effective cloud support engagement requires clearly defined internal processes and designated personnel. questions.title: How do you manage AWS service quotas and constraints?
questions.description: For cloud-based workload architectures, there are service quotas (which are also referred to as service limits). These quotas exist to prevent accidentally provisioning more resources than you need and to limit request rates on API operations so as to protect services from abuse. In mission-critical environments, hitting service quotas or constraints unexpectedly can severely impact operational capabilities and disaster recovery scenarios. There are also resource constraints, for example, the rate that you can push bits down a fiber-optic cable, or the amount of storage on a physical disk. Managing these quotas can be especially important in multi-tenant environments. (Aligns with AWS Well Architected Framework question Reliability #1)

choices.title: Automate quota management

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement automated monitoring and request systems for quota management

helpfulResource.displayText: Implement tools to alert you when thresholds are being approached. You can automate quota increase requests by using AWS Service Quotas APIs.

choices.title: Ensure that a sufficient gap exists between the current quotas and the maximum usage to accommodate failover

improvementPlan.displayText: Calculate and maintain quota buffers that account for failure scenarios including AZ and Regional failures

helpfulResource.displayText: When a resource fails or is inaccessible, that resource might still be counted against a quota until it's successfully terminated. Verify that your quotas cover the overlap of failed or inaccessible resources and their replacements.

choices.title: Monitor and manage quotas

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement regular quota review processes that account for growth projections

helpfulResource.displayText: Evaluate your potential usage and increase your quotas appropriately, allowing for planned growth in usage.

choices.title: Accommodate fixed service quotas and constraints through architecture

improvementPlan.displayText: Review architecture design to ensure compliance with fixed quotas and constraints

helpfulResource.displayText: Be aware of unchangeable service quotas, service constraints, and physical resource limits. Design architectures for applications and services to prevent these limits from impacting reliability.

choices.title: Manage service quotas across accounts and Regions

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish quota management processes across all accounts and regions

helpfulResource.displayText: If you are using multiple accounts or Regions, request the appropriate quotas in all environments in which your production workloads run.

improvementPlan.displayText: Document and maintain awareness of all applicable service quotas and constraints

helpfulResource.displayText: Be aware of your default quotas and manage your quota increase requests for your workload architecture. Know which cloud resource constraints, such as disk or network, are potentially impactful.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this if your workload does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: How do you mitigate deployment risks?
questions.description: In mission-critical environments, deployment risks must be carefully managed to prevent service disruptions that could impact operational capabilities. Adopting approaches that provide fast feedback and enable rapid recovery is essential for maintaining mission readiness. Using these practices mitigates the impact of issues introduced through the deployment of changes. (Aligns with AWS Well Architected Framework question Operational Excellence #6)

choices.title: Automate testing and rollback

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement automated testing and rollback capabilities in both pre-production and production environments.

helpfulResource.displayText: To increase the speed, reliability, and confidence of your deployment process, have a strategy for automated testing and rollback capabilities in pre-production and production environments. Automate testing when deploying to production to simulate human and system interactions that verify the changes being deployed. Automate rollback to revert back to a previous known good state quickly. The rollback should be initiated automatically on pre-defined conditions such as when the desired outcome of your change is not achieved or when the automated test fails. Automating these two activities improves your success rate for your deployments, minimizes recovery time, and reduces the potential impact to the business.

choices.title: Employ safe deployment strategies

improvementPlan.displayText: Implement safe deployment strategies such as feature flags, canary releases, and blue/green deployments.

helpfulResource.displayText: Safe production roll-outs control the flow of beneficial changes with an aim to minimize any perceived impact for customers from those changes. The safety controls provide inspection mechanisms to validate desired outcomes and limit the scope of impact from any defects introduced by the changes or from deployment failures. Safe roll-outs may include strategies such as feature-flags, one-box, rolling (canary releases), immutable, traffic splitting, and blue/green deployments.

choices.title: Test deployments

improvementPlan.displayText: Establish comprehensive pre-production testing using production-equivalent configurations and procedures.

helpfulResource.displayText: Test release procedures in pre-production by using the same deployment configuration, security controls, steps, and procedures as in production. Validate that all deployed steps are completed as expected, such as inspecting files, configurations, and services. Further test all changes with functional, integration, and load tests, along with any monitoring such as health checks. By doing these tests, you can identify deployment issues early with an opportunity to plan and mitigate them prior to production.

choices.title: Plan for unsuccessful changes

improvementPlan.displayText: Develop and document rollback procedures and recovery strategies for all deployment changes.

helpfulResource.displayText: Plan to revert to a known good state, or remediate in the production environment if the deployment causes undesired outcome. Having a policy to establish such a plan helps all teams develop strategies to recover from failed changes. Some example strategies are deployment and rollback steps, change policies, feature flags, traffic isolation, and traffic shifting. A single release may include multiple related component changes. The strategy should provide the ability to withstand or recover from a failure of any component change.

choices.title: None of these

helpfulResource.displayText: Choose this if your workload does not follow these best practices.

questions.title: Do you utilize Chaos Engineering to test and improve workload resilience?
questions.description: Chaos Engineering is a disciplined approach to identifying and addressing system weaknesses before they manifest in production, and is a key component of Continuous Resilience. Continuous Resilience is the ongoing practice of building, validating, and maintaining system resilience through automated testing, monitoring, and improvement cycles. For highly regulated workloads, chaos engineering helps validate system behavior during adversarial conditions and ensures maintained operational capabilities during degraded states. This approach involves deliberately introducing controlled disruptions to verify system resilience, validate failure responses, and improve overall operational readiness.
